title: Bristol photographer captures polar bears and Northern Lights on Arctic adventure
excerpt: Polar bears, the Northern Lights and Arctic landscapes took centre stage in a talk by Bristol-based photographer Ruth Spencer.
content:
Polar bears, the Northern Lights and Arctic landscapes took centre stage in a talk by Bristol-based photographer Ruth Spencer.

The presentation was delivered during a visit to Tyndale Photography Club, where Ms Spencer shared her experiences of photographing wildlife and scenery in Canada and Norway during her talk titled Photography in Cold Climates.

She introduced the talk as a two-part journey, beginning with her travels in Canada before moving on to Norway after a short break.

A spokesperson for Tyndale Photography Club said: "Arriving in Winnipeg, Canada, Ruth took a few days to explore The Riding Mountain National Park in Western Manitoba.

"This allowed her to adjust to the new time zone, shake off the jet lag, get used to the November temperatures and photograph the stunning landscapes of the region."

Following her time in Manitoba, Ms Spencer took a one thousand-mile flight to Churchill, a small town located on the shores of Hudson Bay.

She spent a week in Churchill taking day trips in both a tundra buggy and a Jeep to photograph polar bears.

The club spokesperson said: "She commented that the buggy only offered a top-down perspective whereas the Jeep allowed for ground-level shots with which she was more pleased."

Ms Spencer shared images of playful young males, a mother with her cub, and a solitary bear captured in the cold Arctic environment.

The second half of her talk focused on the Lofoten Islands in Norway, located just inside the Arctic Circle.

She visited in February and March, hoping to capture the Northern Lights.

The spokesperson said: "The breath-taking photos of the snow-blanketed landscapes that Ruth shared were nothing short of incredible.

"Ruth, like many visitors to the region, photographed the striking red buildings of the village of Hamnoy, the yellow buildings in the fishing village of Nusfjord but she was absolutely blown away by the stunning harbour at Henningsvaer, which is framed by the sea and mountains making it an ideal spot for photography."

Ms Spencer also visited Uttakleiv Beach, known for its Devil’s Eye rock pool, another highlight of the region.

She spoke about the challenges of photographing the Northern Lights, describing how the constantly changing intensity and movement make it difficult to capture a focused image.

Despite the challenges, she encouraged the audience to enjoy the moment rather than worry about achieving the perfect shot.

The spokesperson said: "The final image of the evening was almost the final photograph she shot on her Arctic adventure – an absolutely stunning image of Hamnoy beneath a mesmerizing display of the Northern Lights."
